auditor: Claude family, fresh-context same-family audit B
method: Each sampled item's quotations were matched against the cached retrieval (.local/risk-debate/doc) with tools.mjs normalisation and read in about 500 characters of surrounding context. Classification, date, statement, voice and (for replies) target identification were judged against the criteria in propositions.json and the rules in scope.md and drafts/FORMAT.md. Part 2 read every statement, qualification, engagement rationale and missing field of all 198 records and 22 replies, using a term scan plus reading; side counts were computed from pack.json with the rule stated in balance.overall. No source was re-fetched and the proposing pass's verification.json verdicts were not consulted.

coverage.note: All 52 sampled items (30 random, 22 replies) had cached text and every quotation matched. Targeted records were not checked in this audit.

findings.issue: Quotes are verbatim, but the passage does not dispute R01. Pinker's first passage argues that literal-minded goal pursuit (the value-alignment scenario) is self-refuting because intelligence includes interpreting intentions; that targets misspecification, not the independence of intelligence and final goals. His second passage, a designed AI 'could just as easily think like shmoos' / 'no law … ruthless conquistadors', affirms that goals are independent of intelligence, which is R01's thesis. The record's own qualification says so. As supporting evidence for contesting R01, the second item argues the other way.
findings.evidence: popsci text, value-alignment section: 'The ability to choose an action that best satisfies conflicting goals … it is intelligence', followed by 'when we put aside fantasies like foom … artificial intelligence is like any other technology. It is developed incrementally, … tested before it is implemented'. First-fallacy section: 'An artificially intelligent system that was designed rather than evolved could just as easily think like shmoos … There is no law of complex systems …'.
findings.proposed: Re-record as rd-r06-pinker-2018-popsci-fear-robots-contests (engages-premise: that a capable system would pursue a given objective in a way harmful through misunderstanding, and that safety will not come from ordinary incremental testing). Drop the 'conquistadors' item from it, or record that item on R10 (no drive to dominate), where Pinker 2014/2015 already sit. Use 'self-refuting' only as a quoted term.

notes: Overall the pack is close to the balance aim: 91 risk-side and 86 counter-side records.
The overall figure hides proposition-level gaps. The counter side is thin on R07 (4:1), R09 (7:1), R17 (7:2) and R03 (7:3); the risk side is thin on R11 (2:6), R12 (3:7) and R05 (6:10).

R07/R09: the gap is mostly classification, not selection. Texts that dispute extinction-scale or misuse-scale risk are recorded on R11, R12 or R15 under the pairing and 'record once' rules: Richards et al. 2023, Narayanan and Kapoor 2024, Andreessen 2023, Kapoor et al. 2024 (marginal risk), the DAIR statement. A reader of R07 or R09 alone sees almost no dispute. The collection view for R07 and R09 should point to them, or such passages should also be recorded as contesting R07/R09 where they give a reason.

R03/R04/R06: the omissions record that LessWrong and the Alignment Forum refused retrieval, so counter-side texts known to the literature (DavidW 2023, Wentworth 2020, Kokotajlo 2020) are missing. This reflects retrieval, not selection. My verdicts would also turn rd-r06-leike-2022 into context, leaving R06 at 4 risk to 3 counter.
R17: the counter side is thin partly because Hanson 2008 and Gans (2018, 2023) are in the dataset on E04 and linked, not re-recorded. The searchLog supports this.

The counting rule mixes direction with topic. Several 'risk-side' records argue nothing about catastrophe: Widder et al. 2024 (concentration of power, R15), Piantadosi and Hill 2022 (meaning in LLMs, R14), Gwern 2020 and Altman 2024 (scaling, R13). Equally, 'counter-side' records include Christiano 2018 (R16) and Leike 2022 (R06), whose authors elsewhere argue the risk. Report the side counts as passage direction only, never as people or camps; the pack's wording already does this.

Concentration by author is uneven. The three densest risk-side authors (Bengio 13, Bostrom 11, Russell 10) carry 34 records; the densest counter-side authors are Kapoor 9, Narayanan 8, LeCun 6 and Marcus 5. Bengio's count includes his co-authored consensus papers.

Seed coverage on the counter side has gaps. Chollet has no record: his 2017 essay was refused (HTTP 403) and is defined only as a reply target. Melanie Mitchell has context records only. Bender, Gebru et al.'s Stochastic Parrots (2021) was not retrievable, so Bender is represented by Bender and Koller 2020, Bender and Hanna 2023 and the DAIR statement. LeCun's 'A Path Towards Autonomous Machine Intelligence' is unused, and the omissions contradict each other about whether it was retrieved (see packWideFindings). On the risk side every seed author named in the brief is represented by primary text (Yudkowsky deliberately few, because of the dataset).

No stance is attributed from a signature or proximity. All signed statements (CAIS, FLI 2015 and 2023, Mozilla, Meta's statement of support) are recorded as what the text says, with an explicit no-signatory qualification. The DAIR statement lists its three byline authors, which is correct. The one inference about a target is the Howard reply's identification of the TIME article (finding above).

packWideFindings.issue: Duplicate document and source entries for one expression. These split the per-source quotation budget, give one work several ids, and give it inconsistent dateBasis. Andreessen, 'Why AI Will Save the World' has three ids (andreessen-2023-ai-will-save-the-world [publication], andreessen-2023-why-ai-will-save-the-world [posting], andreessen-2023-save-the-world), all for https://a16z.com/ai-will-save-the-world/. Hendrycks et al., 'An Overview of Catastrophic AI Risks' has two (hendrycks-2023-overview-catastrophic, hendrycks-2023-overview; same arXiv v1). Bengio et al., 'Managing AI Risks in an Era of Rapid Progress' has two (bengio-2023-managing-ai-risks, bengio-2023-managing-extreme-risks; sources bengio-2023-managing-ai-risks and takeoff-bengio-2023-managing-extreme-risks; same arXiv v1). Narayanan and Kapoor, 'AI as Normal Technology' has two (narayanan-kapoor-2025-normal-technology, narayanan-2025-normal-technology). Brooks 2014 'AI is a tool, not a threat' appears as two documents for two expressions of the same essay (brooks-2014-tool-not-threat, the Robohub repost; brooks-2014-edge-tool-not-threat, the Edge response).
packWideFindings.proposed: Merge each set into one document, and one source per expression, in the drafts. Re-run the quotation-budget check per merged source. For Brooks, keep one document with two sources (versions), and date it from the earliest dated expression.

packWideFindings.issue: Stale or contradictory omissions.
